correctness.rationale: The cyclotomic factorization gives the exact coin model. The largest coin forces 3 and 5 in support and (q-16)3^(a-1)5^(b-1)q^(c-1)<=1. The three claimed two-prime gap identities follow from a proved coin-gap lemma, proper-divisor totient inequalities, explicit a=1 coin blocks, and matching central gaps. Every power-extension satisfies a verified sufficient interval-overlap criterion for q=7,11,13. Direct exact-arithmetic tests pass; finite checks are not treated as universal proof.

originality.rationale: A complete all-exponent classification of odd phi-practical integers having three distinct prime factors is not stated in the inspected foundational 2011 or 2015 papers or in the targeted research-record searches. Closest two-prime subset-sum and general starter results are carefully distinguished by the missing simultaneous exponent-closure implication. Priority beyond accessible sources remains a risk.
residual_risks: An earlier paper may have deduced the result implicitly as a corollary of more general cyclotomic degree-representation theorems.
The 2015 two-prime subset-sum methods are close enough that priority requires specialist assessment before publication.
Semantic search and inspected documents cannot prove worldwide novelty.

value.rationale: The first nontrivial odd class with exactly three distinct prime supports has a complete sharp structural classification, including all unbounded exponents and a single exceptional squarefree integer. It separates four possible third primes and gives nontrivial exact subset-sum gaps and a uniform power-closure mechanism, with direct use for deciding cyclotomic degree representability.
